Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11 10:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom / internal
Attendees: Sonia, Lena, Ari, Marcus, Jules, Allie, Chris, Priya, Tom

Summary: quick sync to validate Q2 launch readiness, go/no-go checklist status, follow-up from last week's incident, and finalize canary rollout windows. Focus on infra load tests, security signoffs (KMS/SOC2), and release checklist updates.

Topics:
- Incident review blips from 2026-06-04 deploy
- Canary rollout proposal and timings
- 72h load test scope and infra sizing
- Security gaps: KMS/HSM, logging retention, SOC2 items
- Launch playbook updates / rollback procedures

Notes (auto sections may be imperfect):
Action items captured inline; some names may be transcribed incorrectly.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sonia: okay we're gonna start, thanks everyone for jumping on, short agenda, uh, quick incident review first then rollout windows and tests.
[00:12] Lena: hi all, sorry running a bit late on one dependency but I'm here.
[00:15] Ari: morning, quick note, product signoffs are in flight, we need the security checkbox to close before final signoff.
[00:25] Marcus: yep, infra's ready to run large scale tests, we just need the exact traffic profile from product.
[00:30] Sonia: alright let's go through the incident from the 4th — Marcus can you summarize? I put the incident notes in the doc but we can go over highlights.
[00:40] Marcus: sure, so on 2026-06-04 during the reserved capacity deploy we saw a KV cache thrash combined with an unexpected memory spike in the dedicated pool. It manifested as slow tail latency for a subset of tenants. Root cause is interplay between caching TTL drop and a new quantization runtime path, where memory wasn't reclaimed fast enough.
[01:05] Marcus: logs show GC spikes and then some pods hitting OOM, autoscaler did react but slow due to the scale step config. Also, our fallback policy to lighter model variants didn't trigger for a small percentage because the routing policy didn't consider this particular variant mismatch.
[01:25] Priya: just to add, security noticed some noisy audit logging that increased log volume but not a security exposure; it's mostly cost and retention impact, we flagged KMS calls during the incident as higher than normal, but keys were fine.
[01:40] Sonia: ok so two threads: operational (autoscale + memory) and routing + fallback logic. Actionable items? Marcus you mentioned adjusting scale-step config.
[01:50] Marcus: yes, propose bumping the initial replica increment and adding a faster cooldown window for that class of pool. We'll test in canary first.
[02:02] Jules: also adding a step to the launch checklist to verify fallback policy coverage for all model variants in the rollout matrix. We missed one variant mapping that caused the routing gap.
[02:15] Allie: frontend note — when the tail latency spikes, some client side retry logic doubles request volume and that amplifies the problem; we can gate a few flags to reduce parallel retries during canary.
[02:28] Sonia: good catch, Allie, add to action items to toggle those flags in canary.
[02:35] Ari: timeline question — we need to agree canary windows and how long before GA. Product's preference is two 24h canaries spread across two weeks, but infra wants a 72h soak test to capture longer tail behaviours.
[02:50] Marcus: 72h is my ask, because intermittent GC patterns only show up after sustained load. We can do a 72h load test on the dedicated cluster with synthetic traces matching prod QPS.
[03:04] Sonia: ok can we compromise? run the 72h soak on a more isolated dedicated cluster while the public canaries are two 24h windows. That gives both product visibility and infra coverage.
[03:18] Lena: sounds reasonable, but we need to size the soak cluster correctly — today's sizing template may under-provision for peak conditioning. I'll update the sizing to +30% headroom.
[03:30] Marcus: noted. I'll start a sizing run based on last month's QPS and the added headroom.
[03:36] Priya: security — SOC2 checklist: we still have a few open items around KMS/HSM integration notes, key rotation proof, and audit log retention. For launch we need written confirmation that those items are either closed or have compensating controls.
[03:52] Sonia: which ones are blocking? Priya can you list blockers?
[03:55] Priya: sure, main blocker is documented KMS rotation window proof for the private deployment path, and second is the log retention policy alignment with customer contracts. We have mitigation — shorter retention for internal debug logs and long-term archival for audit logs, but need to update the runbook.
[04:12] Sonia: ok please put the final statement in the security doc and drop in the launch folder. We won't block GA if there's a documented compensating control and timeline to fully remediate within the next sprint.
[04:26] Ari: product question — do we have a hard requirement on regional failover for GA or will we roll with single region plus fallback?
[04:34] Lena: for this release we are single-region with cross-region fallback options tested; full multi-region active-active is not in scope. That said we will document the fallback route and test it during canary.
[04:48] Jules: another practical note: support runbook needs a clear triage matrix mapping symptoms to immediate actions (scale up, switch to variant X, toggle flag Y). I'll draft that and share with on-call.
[05:00] Tom: from on-call perspective, please ensure the playbook includes metric thresholds and exact steps to trigger rollback and contacts for on-call escalations. Last time the thresholds were ambiguous which slowed response.
[05:16] Sonia: good, Jules/Tom to sync after this meeting on thresholds.
[05:22] Marcus: back to testing — I propose the following plan: start the 72h soak in a dedicated cluster next Monday 2026-06-15, run synthetic traffic based on the QPS snapshot, and simultaneously run two public canaries (24h each) on 2026-06-16 and 2026-06-23. Canaries use the standard canary ratio 5% traffic first 2 hours then 20% etc, but we'll adjust given risk.
[05:48] Ari: sounds fine, product wants a daily check-in during canaries to review telemetry.
[05:54] Sonia: we'll do a short 20-min post-canary stand each morning the canary is running.
[06:00] Allie: frontend will turn down aggressive retries and ensure feature flags are in place. We'll provide a list of flags by EOD.
[06:08] Priya: I'll get the SOC2/KMS summary by 2026-06-16 and drop it in the security folder.
[06:14] Jules: I'll update the launch checklist, add the fallback mapping item, and include the incident learnings. Targeting 2026-06-15.
[06:22] Sonia: great — one more item: pricing/units on dedicated vs hosted — finance requested a short note on expected unit cost delta during canary vs GA for the launch doc. Ari can you take that?
[06:33] Ari: yes I'll work with finance, can have a short delta note by 2026-06-14.
[06:40] Chris: small infra ops ask — when you run the soak please ensure we snapshot kernel and driver versions so we can reproduce the memory pattern if needed.
[06:50] Marcus: absolutely, we will capture full node snapshots and attach to the soak run artifact.
[06:56] Sonia: ok let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[07:00] Sonia: recap: Marcus run 72h soak starting 6/15, capture node snapshots; Marcus update scale-step config ticket; Jules update launch checklist and playbook; Priya finalize SOC2/KMS summary; Allie toggle frontend retry flags for canary; Sonia finalize canary schedule and post to channel; Ari provide cost delta note; Lena update sizing +30%.
[07:26] Sonia: any blockers we missed?
[07:29] Tom: none from on-call, just need the thresholds in playbook.
[07:32] All: no.
[07:35] Sonia: great, I'll send calendar invites for the canary check-ins and update the launch folder. Thanks everyone.

Closing notes: transcript contains occasional mis-hearings — e.g., 'KV cache' rendered as 'K V cache' in some exported lines; product names sometimes split.
